bib.title: Muse: Text-To-Image Generation via Masked Generative Transformers

read.skipped: Reference list (lines 852-1034) skimmed only, not read entry by entry

question: Can a masked-token transformer with parallel decoding, conditioned on a frozen LLM, match diffusion and autoregressive text-to-image quality at far lower inference cost?
hypothesis: Conditioning on a pre-trained LLM embedding and predicting masked discrete image tokens in parallel gives high quality with fewer sampling steps; LLM embeddings are roughly linearly mappable to vision representations.
contributions: State-of-the-art text-to-image model with excellent FID and CLIP scores
Significantly faster than comparable models due to quantized image tokens and parallel decoding
Out-of-the-box zero-shot editing: inpainting, outpainting, mask-free editing

method.summary: Frozen T5-XXL encoder embeds text; a VQGAN tokenizes images to discrete tokens; a base masked transformer predicts masked 16x16 tokens (256x256 image) with cross-entropy, and a super-res transformer maps them to 64x64 tokens (512x512). Inference uses iterative parallel decoding with cosine schedule and classifier-free guidance.

datasets.name: Imagen dataset
datasets.source: Saharia et al., 2022 (provided by Imagen authors)

datasets.name: CC3M
datasets.split: models trained on CC3M for Table 1

models.name: Muse base (largest)
models.architecture: masked transformer with self-attn, cross-attn to text, MLP

models.name: Muse super-res
models.architecture: 32 multi-axis transformer layers plus 16-layer low-res encoder

models.name: T5-XXL encoder
models.architecture: frozen text encoder, 4096-d embeddings linearly projected

training.objective: cross-entropy on masked image tokens; variable masking rate (arccos, mean 0.64); text dropped on 10% of samples for CFG
training.regularisation: no online EMA; offline EMA over checkpoints every 5000 steps, decay 0.7

other.decoder_finetune: VQGAN decoder widened (4 residual blocks per resolution, base channels 256) and fine-tuned with encoder, codebook and transformers frozen

inference.decoding: iterative parallel masked decoding, cosine schedule, highest-confidence tokens unmasked per step
inference.samples: 16 images per prompt, best by CLIP score chosen (Fig 6 and human eval); FID sampling parameter sets not fully stated

parameters.guidance: t linearly increased during sampling; value for reported FID not stated

other.negative_prompt: replace unconditional logit with negative-prompt logit

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance, quality and diversity

metrics.name: Human alignment preference
metrics.definition: 'Which image matches with the caption better?' 5 raters, >=3 consensus

metrics.name: Inference time
metrics.definition: per-batch time on TPUv4 (A100 for SD/LDM)

eval.protocol: CC3M FID with models trained on CC3M; COCO zero-shot; no seeds or error bars; human eval on PartiPrompts vs SD v1.4 only

evidence.quote: Per-batch inference time for several models.

results.claim: Muse-3B reaches zero-shot COCO FID-30K 7.88 at 256x256, slightly better than Parti-3B (8.10).
results.setup: Zero-shot MS-COCO, 256x256, Muse-3B trained on the Imagen dataset (460M pairs); Parti-3B number from Table 2
results.quote: Our 3B model achieves an FID score of 7.88 which is slightly better than the score of 8.1 achieved by the Parti-3B model

results.claim: Muse-3B takes 0.5 s at 256x256 versus 6.4 s for Parti-3B (Table 3 is labelled per-batch time; batch size not given).
results.setup: Table 3 'Per-batch inference time'; Muse, Imagen, Parti benchmarked internally on TPUv4; batch size and what a batch contains not stated
results.note: Caption says per-batch; Fig 1 caption says 'Each image was generated in 1.3s on a TPUv4 chip' for 512x512 (Table 3 also lists 1.3s). Whether 0.5s is per image or per batch is not defined.
results.table: Table 3, row Muse-3B 256x256, column Time (0.5s); row Parti-3B 256x256 (6.4s)

results.claim: Muse decodes 256 tokens in 24 steps in the base model and 4096 tokens in 8 steps in the super-res model.
results.setup: Iterative parallel decoding with cosine schedule choosing a fixed fraction of the highest-confidence masked tokens per step
results.quote: we are able to perform inference of 256 tokens using only 24 decoding steps in our base model and 4096 tokens using 8 decoding steps in our super-resolution model

results.claim: Muse estimated more than 10x faster than Imagen-3B or Parti-3B and 3x faster than Stable Diffusion v1.4.
results.setup: Comparisons on similar hardware (TPU-v4), same image size; SD benchmark from Lambda Labs on A100 GPUs, so hardware is not matched for SD
results.quote: we estimate that Muse is more than 10x faster at inference time than either Imagen-3B or Parti-3B models

results.claim: Muse (632M base + 268M super-res) gets CC3M FID 6.06, SOTA.
results.setup: Trained and evaluated on CC3M; baseline best prior Draft-and-revise 9.65
results.quote: Our 632M(base)+268M(super-res) parameter model achieves a state of the art FID score of 6.06

results.claim: Muse-3B CLIP score 0.32 on COCO versus 0.27 reported in Imagen.
results.setup: Zero-shot COCO 256x256; text elsewhere cites 0.29 for Imagen at much higher FID (about 20)
results.note: Text in Sec 3.2 says Imagen's CLIP is 0.29 (at FID about 20) and about 0.27 at FID 7.27; Table 2 caption says 0.27.
results.quote: Muse achieves a CLIP score of 0.32, higher than the score of 0.27 reported in Imagen.

results.claim: Human raters judged Muse-3B better aligned than Stable Diffusion v1.4 on 70.6% of PartiPrompts (SD 25.4%, no consensus 4%), about 2.7x.
results.setup: PartiPrompts, 1650 prompts; 5 raters per pair; at least 3-rater consensus required; 16 images generated per prompt, highest-CLIP one used (paper does not say outright it applied to both models); SD via CompVis notebook
results.quote: Muse was chosen as better aligned than Stable Diffusion for 70.6% of the prompts, Stable Diffusion was chosen as better aligned than Muse for 25.4%

results.claim: Best-of-16 by CLIP score was used for the human evaluation and the qualitative figures, so these results are reranked samples.
results.quote: For each prompt, 16 image instances were generated, and the one with the highest CLIP score (Radford et al., 2021) was used.

results.claim: Base model expected masking rate is 0.64 under the truncated arccos distribution.
results.setup: Training masking rate r sampled from p(r)=2/pi (1-r^2)^(-1/2)
results.quote: This has an expected masking rate of 0.64, with a strong bias towards higher masking rates.

results.claim: Classifier-free guidance uses logits l_g=(1+t)l_c - t l_u with text dropped on 10% of training samples; guidance scale t is increased linearly during sampling to reduce diversity loss.
results.setup: Applied per masked token at inference
results.quote: At training time, we remove text conditioning on 10% of samples chosen randomly

results.claim: Zero-shot mask-free editing resamples 8% of tokens per iteration for 100 iterations with guidance scale 4 and top-k 3.
results.setup: Low-res base model, then super-res on final output
results.quote: we resample 8% of the tokens per iteration for 100 iterations, with a guidance scale of 4

results.claim: Muse is weak at long phrase rendering, high cardinality and multiple cardinalities.
results.quote: prompts indicating high object cardinality tend to result in generated images which do not correctly reflect that desired cardinality (e.g., rendering only 7 wine bottles when the prompt specified 10)

results.claim: Larger VQGAN codebooks gave no improvement; codebook size 8192.
results.setup: Base tokenizer CNN with 19 ResNet blocks
results.quote: Larger codebook sizes did not result in performance improvements.

results.claim: A language model learned from scratch did much worse than frozen T5-XXL, especially on long prompts and rare words.
results.quote: found that performance was signiﬁcantly worse than using a pre-trained LLM, especially on long prompts and rare words

results.claim: Base model training length is printed as 1M steps in the text and 1.5M steps in Table 4.
results.note: Table 4 prints Training steps 1.5M; Table 6 (super-res) prints 1M.
results.quote: Training is performed for 1M steps, with a batch size of 512 on 512-core TPU-v4 chips

limits: Fails at long multi-word phrase rendering, high cardinality, multiple cardinalities (Sec 3.1).
No realism human evaluation, argued to be only valid between models of similar alignment (Sec 3.2.2).
Speed comparison mixes hardware: Muse/Imagen/Parti on TPUv4, SD/LDM on A100 from a third-party benchmark; batch size not given.
Faster diffusion methods (progressive distillation, better ODE solvers) not compared (Sec 2.8).
Code and demo not released for misuse/bias reasons; dataset biases acknowledged.
Human eval compares only against SD v1.4 with best-of-16 CLIP reranking.
Training steps inconsistent: text 1M vs Table 4 1.5M.
